system_prompt: You are an expert code reviewer. Analyze the provided codebase for bugs, security issues, and correctness problems. Provide actionable feedback. All files are located in /tmp/files
task_prompt: You are an expert code reviewer. Your task is to analyze the Joi codebase. Joi is a JavaScript schema validation library that validates values against schemas. The codebase handles schema compilation, validation pipeline (sync and async), LRU caching of validation results, state and path tracking, references and ancestor resolution, conditional schemas (when), type coercion, and type-specific rules (string, number, date, array, object, etc.). Your goal is to identify bugs, correctness issues, boundary condition errors, logic errors, off-by-one mistakes, missing validation checks, cache invalidation or key consistency issues, indexing errors (e.g. 0-based vs 1-based), units or format handling mistakes, and any other issues that could affect reliability or correctness. Write your findings to /tmp/outputs/review.md

rubric.criterion: Identifies the assert message/options bug in lib/index.js in internals.assert where when the third argument (args[0]) is an object the code sets message = args[0] (treating the options object as the message), so assert(value, schema, { abortEarly: false }) passes the options object as the error message and options become undefined, losing user options

Identifies the cleanup-on-success-only bug in lib/validator.js in internals.entry where cleanup (schema.$_root.untrace()) is called only when !result.error, so on validation error cleanup is skipped and trace state leaks or becomes inconsistent for the next validation

Identifies the number coerce trim order bug in lib/types/number.js in the coerce method where value.trim() is called after parseFloat(value) instead of before, so the string passed to parseFloat and used in the unsafe check still has leading/trailing spaces and the unsafe or normalizeDecimal comparison can fail for trimmed numeric strings

Identifies the prefs cache return bug in lib/validator.js in internals.prefs where when schema._preferences[Common.symbols.prefs] is set the code returns it without checking isDefaultOptions, so a later validation with different options still receives the first validation's cached merged prefs and user options are ignored

Identifies the refs loop control-flow bug in lib/values.js in Values.get where when resolved === undefined the code uses break instead of continue, so after the first ref that resolves to undefined the loop stops and a later ref that would match is never checked, causing valid values to be rejected when using .valid(ref) or .allow(ref) with multiple refs

Identifies the stripUnknown condition bug in lib/types/keys.js in internals.unknown where the condition uses !prefs.stripUnknown instead of prefs.stripUnknown, so the strip/skip block is entered when stripUnknown is false and unknown keys are never stripped when the user passes stripUnknown: true

Identifies the sync entry prefs bug in lib/validator.js in exports.entry where when prefs is provided the code asserts on warnings/artifacts but never calls Common.preferences(Common.defaults, prefs), so settings stays Common.defaults and user options (abortEarly, stripUnknown, etc.) are ignored for sync validation

Identifies the template fallback order bug in lib/errors.js in exports.template where when messages[code] is missing the code returns messages[code] (undefined) and the final return is messages['*'] instead of messages[code], so the specific code message is never returned and the wildcard is always used when reaching that branch
